```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

The discard **raising** side of the package, end to end: the groups of strata
that are raised together - and the data each group's discard rate is estimated
from - are written out by hand. It is a walkthrough, not a test: nothing here
asserts pass or fail, and it is the script to run chunk by chunk in RStudio.

This is vignette **2** of three: **1** explored the data, and **3** allocates the
raised catch to lengths and ages. The first sections produce the real
deliverable; the last compares it with an alternative way of raising.

It is driven directly with the vendored RDBESStockCoord functions -
`check_group_conditions()` and `catchRaising()` - the same pattern ICES's own
discard-raising scripts use: a named list of quosures per method
(`strataCond` = which strata a group claims, `matchedDataCond` = which data its
discard rate is estimated from), checked, then raised. Nothing wraps that
call.

The last two sections give the two output data sets this whole vignette
exists for:

* **CC** (Catch Combined) - one row per `catchCategory`, the stock-wide raised
  total, in the format of the stock coordination (SCF v3): `catchCombined()`
  makes it;
* **CAR / CAS** - every raised row, and the donor strata behind each group's
  rate,

the second following the schema of a real ICES stock-annex CAR / CAS export.
CAR and CAS are built inline, as plain data frames, on purpose - not wrapped in
functions and not written to csv yet. Once the shape is right, both become
functions that build and save these data sets; that is future work.

# Data

Brill, `bll.27.3a47de`, 2025, from the CEF csv file under
`inst/extdata/data_CEF_format` (local to this machine; the file is not in the
repository). Only the catch table is needed for raising.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rcef)

cef_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "data_CEF_format" )

# blank cells (no discard domain, no trip count ...) read as NA
catch_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "2024", "bll_2024_catches_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                       na.strings = "")

catch_data_BMS <- catch_data %>% 
  filter (catchCategory != "Dis")

catch_data <- catch_data %>% 
  filter (catchCategory != "BMS")


```

`derive_fields()` is what turns raw CEF into strata-ready data: it parses
`metier4` (and `target`, `mesh`, `metier4_mesh`) out of `fleetValue` and the ICES area
levels out of `areaValue`. Country and season are already their own
columns - `vesselFlagCountry` and `seasonValue` - so there is nothing to
derive for those two. It runs once, here: from this point on the tables, the
plots and the groups read the columns `catch_data` has and derive nothing, so a
column you add - or regroup - is used as you left it.

```{r derive}
catch_data <- derive_fields(catch_data)
nrow(catch_data)
```

Nothing else is derived: the groups' conditions are plain `metier4` /
`catchCategory` / `fleetValue` tests against `catch_data` as loaded, and the
CAR and CAS sections compute their own landings and discard sums directly off it.

# The groups

Hand-written quosures, checked and raised with `check_group_conditions()` and
`catchRaising()` directly.

These are the same six groups as the RDBESStockCoord example this is based on
(that example calls the gear column `gear`; `derive_fields()` names the same
thing `metier4`, so the conditions here use `metier4`). G1-G3 split the main
gears, G4 is a REST group for everything else, G5 pulls out the `fleetValue`
sentinel for incidental bycatch (IBC), G6 is BMS on its own - between them
every row is claimed exactly once, discards or not.

```{r strata-cond}
strataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = quo(metier4 == "TBB" & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G2 = quo(metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G3 = quo(metier4 %in% c("OTB", "SSC", "SDN") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G4 = quo(!metier4 %in% c("TBB", "GTR", "GNS", "OTB", "SSC", "SDN") &
             catchCategory != "BMS" & fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC"),
  G5 = quo(fleetValue == "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" & catchCategory != "BMS"))

strataCond_manual_BMS <- list(
  G6 = quo(catchCategory == "BMS"))
```

`matchedDataCond`: G1-G3, G5 and G6 are raised on their own strata (the same
condition, reused). G4 (REST) has too little discard data of its own and draws
on every gear instead - minus five strata whose own discard ratio the source
example flagged as implausible (verified present in this bll 2025 data too:
Sweden / 27.3.a.21 and France / 27.7.e both occur). Remove the `!(...)` block
to see their effect on G4's rate.

```{r matched-cond}
matchedDataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = strataCond_manual$G1,
  G2 = strataCond_manual$G2,
  G3 = strataCond_manual$G3,
  G4 = quo(catchCategory != "BMS" &
             fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" &
             !((vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                  fleetValue == "GNS_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 3)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 4)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "France" & areaValue == "27.7.e" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_100-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 2) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_90-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 3) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_70-89_2_35_all" & seasonValue == 1))),
  G5 = strataCond_manual$G5)


matchedDataCond_manual_BMS <- list(
  G6 = strataCond_manual_BMS$G6)
```

## Condition diagnostics

`check_group_conditions()` is what `catchRaising()` runs internally before it
raises anything; running it separately is the "optional, automatically run
with raising, but good practice" step of the RDBESStockCoord scripts - every
stratum is checked for both a gap (claimed by no group) and an overlap
(claimed twice) before any weight moves. The engine prints a "Condition
diagnostics" banner for each condition; it is hidden here.

```{r check, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = strataCond_manual,
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                                  conditionType = "matched_data",
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)


cond_st <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data_BMS,
                                  condition_list = strataCond_manual_BMS,
                                  domain = "domainCatchBMS",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data_BMS,
                                  condition_list = matchedDataCond_manual_BMS,
                                  conditionType = "matched_data",
                                  domain = "domainCatchBMS",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
```

Both counts should be 0, and the column sums say how many rows each group
claims:

```{r check-result}
strata_matrix <- do.call(cbind, cond_st)
cat(sprintf("manual: %d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) > 1)))
colSums(strata_matrix)
```

## Raise the catch

`catchRaising()` prints its own banner per condition pair, unconditionally
(the check above, run again internally) - that noise is the engine's own
logging, hidden here as well.

```{r raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
raised_manual <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                              condition_raising_st_list = strataCond_manual,
                              condition_matched_data_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                              type = "discards",
                              originType = "WGEstimate",
                              variableType = "WeightLive",
                              logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))


try(raised_manual_BMS <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data_BMS,
                              condition_raising_st_list = strataCond_manual_BMS,
                              condition_matched_data_list = matchedDataCond_manual_BMS,
                              type = "BMS",
                              originType = "WGEstimate",
                              variableType = "WeightLive",
                              logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
)
```

```{r raise-result}
cat(sprintf("manual raising: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_manual),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

# Overview of the raised weight

Imported against raised, at any aggregation. `plot_catches()` is the plot of
the catch weight, for any catch - raw, or raised as here. It takes any
catch-side column on `x` and an optional `facet`: landings / discards are the
fill, imported / raised is the mark (solid = imported, transparent and
hatched = raised), and whatever you put on `x` or `facet` is the aggregation.
The title says what the catch holds: *imported + raised* here; a catch in which
nothing was raised is titled *only imported* and has no mark, as in vignette 1.
`catchCategory` narrows it to just
`"Lan"` or `"Dis"`, useful whenever one of the two makes the other hard to see.

```{r overview-table}
raised_overview_table(raised_manual)
```

By metier:

```{r overview-metier, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by metier"}
plot_catches(catch = raised_manual, x = "vesselFlagCountry", facet = "metier4",catchCategory = "Dis", ncol = 5)
```

By metier, faceted by country - a finer aggregation than the group
definitions themselves ever used:

```{r overview-country, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by metier, one panel per country"}
plot_catches(catch = raised_manual, x = "metier4", facet = "vesselFlagCountry")
```

# Discard rate across the raising groups

Not how much weight moved, but whether the *strata a group draws its rate
from* agree with each other. `plot_DR()` is the discard rate per stratum -
the plot of vignette 1 for raw catch - and given the raised catch it draws one
point per raw stratum, a **circle** where its discards came with the data
(imported, i.e. sampled) and a **cross** where the raising added them; the
title says the strata are *imported + raised*. Put the raising **group** on
`x` (`"DrGroup"`): a group's crosses all sit on one line, the rate
it was raised at, and its circles show how far the strata it was built
from scatter around that line - a group whose circles run from 2% to
40% is a guess dressed up as a group, no matter how plausible its raised
rate looks.

Once strata are raised the crosses are the reference, so the
weighted-mean line and the per-point labels of the raw plot are left out. Only
the strata of the raised catch are drawn, so a group raised from a pool wider than its own
strata - G4, the rest of the gears - shows its donors under the groups they
belong to rather than under G4.

```{r donors-plot, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of every stratum of the raised catch by raising group, circles where imported and crosses where raised, coloured by metier"}
plot_DR(catch = raised_manual,
        x = "DrGroup", colour = "metier4", rate = "rate")
```

Imported and raised side by side instead of as the mark: `importedOrRaised`
is a variable like any other, so it can be a `facet` (or the `colour`, the
`shape`, the `x`) - and is then not drawn as the mark as well.

```{r dr-facet-status, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of every stratum by metier, coloured by country, one panel for the imported strata and one for the raised"}
plot_DR(catch = raised_manual, x = "metier4", colour = "vesselFlagCountry",
        facet = "importedOrRaised", rate = "rate")
```

# Output: CC (Catch Combined)

One row per `catchCategory`, the stock-wide raised total. The headline number
this vignette exists to produce: total landings and total (sampled + raised)
discards for the stock, in tonnes. One row per `catchCategory` actually
present in `raised_manual` - usually `Lan` and `Dis`, but `BMS` too if the
stock reports it; nothing below is hardcoded to just those two.

`catchCombined()` adds the raised catch up and writes it in the format of the
stock coordination (SCF v3): the year, the working group and the stock come
straight off the data, every field of the format the data does not fill is
there, empty, and `unit = "t"` is the tonnes the format wants. Take one
origin - `originType_catch = "WGEstimate"` is the working group's own catch,
the raised discards among it; a stratum the raising had no rate for (`NaN`)
adds up as nothing. Its pair for the lengths and ages, `distributionsCombined()`,
is in vignette 3.

`car_version`, `car_version_desc` and `car_scheme_name` identify *this*
allocation scheme's run - a different scheme (another set of groups) would
carry a different version, so several runs'
CC / CAR / CAS outputs can sit in the same downstream table without being
confused for each other. The first two are the `version` and
`versionDescription` of the CC, and all three are reused as they are in the
next section - keep every use in sync if any of them changes.

```{r cc}
car_version      <- 1
car_version_desc <- "Manual_Stock_Annex"
car_scheme_name  <- "Stock_Annex"

cc_out <- catchCombined(catch_data = raised_manual,
                        grouping = "catchCategory",
                        originType_catch = "WGEstimate",
                        variableType_catch = "WeightLive",
                        unit = "t", round = 3,
                        version = car_version, versionDescription = car_version_desc)
cc_out[, c("recordType", "version", "year", "stock", "catchCategory",
           "variableType", "variableUnit", "total")]
```

# Output: CAR and CAS (detailed)

Two tables sharing one allocation-scheme identity (`recordType`, `version`,
`versionDescription` and `catchAllocationSchemeName` line up between them, the
same values the CC section already set) - kept as two separate data frames
for now, per-row CAR and per-donor-stratum CAS. Combining them into one csv
with CAS appended under CAR, and writing either to disk, is future work.

## CAR: every row `catchRaising()` produced

Each row is tagged with the **group** that raised it. `catchAllocationGroupName`
is filled *only* where a row was actually raised - `imported` is Y / N,
matching the source RDBESStockCoord convention rather than rcef's own
"imported" / "raised" wording, and it is that column, not the group name, that
marks a row as sampled. The group itself is rebuilt here by re-testing every
row against `strataCond_manual` - the same partition `check_group_conditions()`
already confirmed above is exhaustive and non-overlapping, so exactly one
group matches every row, imported or raised alike (the engine's own `DrGroup`
column agrees, and is filled the same way on both - it is `.car_group` below,
not `DrGroup`, that is blanked back out on imported rows, only because the CAR
schema itself only names a group where raising actually happened).

```{r car}
raised_manual <- raised_manual %>%
  mutate(.car_group = case_when(
    !!strataCond_manual$G1 ~ "G1",
    !!strataCond_manual$G2 ~ "G2",
    !!strataCond_manual$G3 ~ "G3",
    !!strataCond_manual$G4 ~ "G4",
    !!strataCond_manual$G5 ~ "G5",
    # !!strataCond_manual$G6 ~ "G6",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# the engine's own DrGroup agrees with the re-test on every raised row
with(subset(raised_manual, importedOrRaised == "raised"),
     all(DrGroup == .car_group))

car_out <- raised_manual %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAR",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         catchAllocationGroupName = if_else(importedOrRaised == "raised",
                                            .car_group, NA_character_),
         imported = if_else(importedOrRaised == "imported", "Y", "N")) %>%
  select(-.car_group, -importedOrRaised) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAR: %d rows x %d columns (%d imported, %d raised across %d groups)\n",
            nrow(car_out), ncol(car_out),
            sum(car_out$imported == "Y"), sum(car_out$imported == "N"),
            n_distinct(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

`car_out` carries the scheme identity columns first, then every column of the
raised table. The raised rows first, key columns only:

```{r car-head}
car_out %>%
  arrange(desc(imported == "N"), catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, imported, vesselFlagCountry, seasonValue,
         areaValue, fleetValue, catchCategory, total) %>%
  head(10)
```

## Which strata are raised from which group

`raised_manual$.car_group`, built above, already tags every row with its
group - nothing new to derive. `plot_river()` draws it as an alluvial: metier
on the left, raising group on the right, ribbon width the landings weight -
the same "how much of the stock comes from which pool" question the CAR/CAS
tables answer in numbers, here in one picture. Landings only (`catchCategory`
is not itself a raising outcome, and counting discards too would double the
weight of a raised stratum against an imported one).

```{r river, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Alluvial plot of landings weight flowing from each metier to its raising group"}
raised_manual %>%
  filter(catchCategory == "Lan") %>%
  mutate(.landings_t = total / 1000) %>%
  plot_river(left_var = "metier4", right_var = ".car_group", value_var = ".landings_t")
```

## CAS: the donor strata behind each group's rate

Only the imported `Dis` rows that satisfy at least one group's
`matchedDataCond` - the ones `catchRaising()` actually pulled a rate from.
Unlike CAR, this is **not** a partition: G4's `matchedDataCond` draws on every
gear (see the manual grouping above), so a stratum that is G1's own donor is
*also* one of G4's many donors - it appears once *per group it feeds*, not once
per row.

`weightingTotal` and `rate` are per this stratum, matched on `domainCatchDis` -
the column CEF itself uses to link a `Dis` estimate to its domain:
`weightingTotal` is that domain's own landed weight (kg, same unit as `total` -
unlike the CC table, CAR and CAS stay in the CEF's native kg throughout), and
`rate` is this row's discards over that landed weight (discards / landings,
*not* the raising side's `discard_rate` = discards / (landings + discards) -
matching the source RDBESStockCoord convention's unbounded `dis_ratio`, and
the same `rate` `build_coverage_strata()` and `plot_DR()` use,
confirmed against the reference CAR-CAS_detailed.csv: its `rate` column is
exactly `total / weightingTotal`, occasionally above 1).

```{r cas}
landings_by_domain <- catch_data %>%
  filter(catchCategory == "Lan", originType == "WGEstimate",
         variableType == "WeightLive", !is.na(domainCatchDis)) %>%
  group_by(domainCatchDis) %>%
  summarise(.landings = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cas_out <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matchedDataCond_manual), function(g)
  catch_data %>%
    filter(!!matchedDataCond_manual[[g]], catchCategory == "Dis",
           !is.na(domainCatchDis), originType == "WGEstimate",
           variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
    mutate(catchAllocationGroupName = g))) %>%
  left_join(landings_by_domain, by = "domainCatchDis") %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAS",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         imported = "Y",
         weightingCategory = "Lan",
         weightingParameter = "WeightLive",
         averagingMethod = "weighted",
         weightingTotal = round(.landings, 3),
         rate = round(total / .landings, 4)) %>%
  select(-.landings) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAS: %d donor rows x %d columns across %d groups (%d distinct strata - some strata donate to more than one group)\n",
            nrow(cas_out), ncol(cas_out), n_distinct(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName),
            n_distinct(cas_out$domainCatchDis)))
```

The first donor rows, key columns only:

```{r cas-head}
cas_out %>%
  arrange(catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, vesselFlagCountry, areaValue, fleetValue,
         domainCatchDis, total, weightingTotal, rate) %>%
  head(10)
```

## Do CAR and CAS describe the same groups?

Every group CAR raised something for should have at least one CAS donor row,
and vice versa - the two tables describing the same groups, not two different
countings. A group *can* legitimately fail this (this data's G5 / IBC does):
`catchRaising()` and every donor filter above are restricted to
`originType == "WGEstimate"`, so a group whose own discard records all carry
some *other* `originType` (IBC's here are all `"Official"`) has no
`WGEstimate` donor at all - CAS then has no row for it, and its CAR rows
raised on nothing get `total = NaN`, not a real weight. That is a genuine gap
in the **scheme** (this group cannot really be raised as defined), not a bug
in these tables - so it is printed by name below, never just a silent `FALSE`.

```{r linked}
car_groups <- na.omit(unique(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName))
cas_groups <- unique(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName)
ok_linked <- setequal(car_groups, cas_groups)
cat(sprintf("every CAR group also appears in CAS, and vice versa: %s\n", ok_linked))
if (!ok_linked) {
  raised_no_donor  <- setdiff(car_groups, cas_groups)
  donor_not_raised <- setdiff(cas_groups, car_groups)
  if (length(raised_no_donor))
    cat(sprintf("  raised in CAR but no CAS donor (raised total is NaN - check originType): %s\n",
                paste(raised_no_donor, collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(donor_not_raised))
    cat(sprintf("  donor in CAS but nothing raised under it in CAR: %s\n",
                paste(donor_not_raised, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

`cc_out`, `car_out` and `cas_out` are plain data frames in this session;
nothing was written to a file.

# Comparing two ways of raising

What does changing the groups change? The groups above are the stock-annex
ones: G4, the rest of the gears, draws its discard rate on every gear. Write
the same strata with every group drawing only on its **own** strata and raise
again - `matchedDataCond` is the only thing that changes. (G5, the incidental
bycatch, has no `WGEstimate` donor of its own, so it is raised on nothing in
both: its raised rows come out as `NaN`.)

```{r own-raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
matchedDataCond_own <- strataCond_manual    # every group draws on its own strata only

raised_own <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                           condition_raising_st_list = strataCond_manual,
                           condition_matched_data_list = matchedDataCond_own,
                           type = "discards",
                           originType = "WGEstimate",
                           variableType = "WeightLive",
                           logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

`raised_overview_table()` and `plot_compare_raised()` compare raised catches
directly: give them two or more, written `list(a, b)` or `c(a, b)`, and
nothing else is needed. A scheme is called after its object unless you name it,
as below. Imported against raised, by catch category, for both in one table -
the schemes of one figure sit next to each other so it reads across. A raised
row whose group had no donor to draw a rate from comes out of the raising as
`NaN`; it raises to nothing and counts as no weight, and the `No donor (rows)`
column counts those rows wherever there are any.

```{r overview-compare}
raised_overview_table(c(annex = raised_manual, own = raised_own))
```

Add `by` to aggregate at any other level - a season, a metier, an area, the
raising group - and every figure, Total included, is split by it:

```{r overview-compare-by}
raised_overview_table(c(annex = raised_manual, own = raised_own), by = "DrGroup")
```

The same comparison drawn. For each level of `x` there is one bar per scheme
(the colour), imported weight solid and raised weight transparent and hatched; `facet`
splits it further and `catchCategory` keeps just the landings or the discards,
which are otherwise dwarfed by the landings.

```{r compare-metier, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Discards by metier, one bar per scheme, imported solid and raised hatched"}
plot_compare_raised(c(annex = raised_manual, own = raised_own),
                    x = "metier4", catchCategory = "Dis")
```

By country, one panel per season - a finer aggregation than the group
definitions themselves ever used:

```{r compare-country, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Discards by country, one panel per season, one bar per scheme"}
plot_compare_raised(c(annex = raised_manual, own = raised_own),
                    x = "vesselFlagCountry", facet = "seasonValue",
                    catchCategory = "Dis")
```

And whether the strata a group draws its rate from agree with each other,
for the alternative: with every group on its own strata, each group's circles
are exactly the strata it was raised from.

